items.claim: The span's bytes are one syntactically continuous sentence rather than atomic sayings cohering, so proverb_cluster mis-types the unit the row itself describes.
items.grounds: Byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map: 6:12 carries the run's only nominal subject, אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן , and its first participial predicate, ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה ; 6:13 is entirely dependent - קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו - three participial forms with prepositional phrases, carrying no subject noun and no prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, and 6:14 continues under the same third-person masculine singular reference, תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ , before the apodosis opens at 6:15 with עַל כֵּ֗ן . The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the form reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings: WEB renders 6:13 as bare relative clauses depending on 6:12, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13). A proverb_cluster row claims that atomic sayings cohere as one unit; these member verses are not separable sayings, since 6:13 cannot stand as a saying at all, and the row's own rationale describes the span as one cumulative portrait resolved by a causal clause. The collection's ruled precedent types a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning verses as one proverb-unit regardless of verse count, which is the byte situation here. The span itself is not in question: the causal opener at 6:15 ties the apodosis back to 6:12, a petuchah closes oshb:Prov.6.15 in WLC (tier-3, single-witness, inventory-confirmed), and 6:16 opens the numerical formula.
items.proposed_change: Field repair, span Prov.6.12-Prov.6.15 unchanged: retype unit_type and literature_type_guess from proverb_cluster to single_proverb under the ruled continuous-sentence precedent (one syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one proverb-unit regardless of verse count), and re-open the dependent fields a driver swap re-opens - strongest_rejected_alternative, which must then reject the cluster reading on the dependency bytes of 6:13 rather than on the count of verses, plus confidence, observed_substrate_signals and the device_notes deviation sentence. If the adjudicator instead holds that the three participial clauses of 6:13 are separately quotable sayings, proverb_cluster stands and only the rejection sentence needs its byte ground restated; either way this is a type repair, not a span change.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived both ways at byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map. The finding's form reading holds: oshb:Prov.6.12 (7 words) carries the nominal subject אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן and the first participial predicate ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה; oshb:Prov.6.13 (6 words) reads קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו, three participial forms each with a prepositional phrase, without a subject noun or a prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, so it cannot stand as a saying, and WEB renders it as dependent relative clauses, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13); oshb:Prov.6.14 (9 words; 1 K/Q note in pmarks_Prov.json, the inline ketiv מדנים before the qere מִדְיָנִ֥ים; 1 paseq seg, count-only) continues the same third-person singular reference from תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ to its finite verb יְשַׁלֵּֽחַ; and oshb:Prov.6.15 opens the apodosis with עַל כֵּ֗ן (that pointing 1 verse book-wide at byte tier; skeleton 2 verses, Prov.6.15 and Prov.7.15), “Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.” (web:Prov.6.15). The shipped row itself describes the span as a chain of participial clauses sharing one grammatical subject and resolved by the causal clause, yet rejects single_proverb because the cohesion runs across four verses rather than a single couplet - a verse-count ground that the ruled continuous-sentence precedent (one syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one proverb-unit typed single_proverb regardless of verse count) expressly removes - while proverb_cluster asserts atomic sayings cohering, which none of these member verses are. Warrant defect, not load-bearing: the span is untouched. Both sides weighed from bytes: the preceding unit closes at oshb:Prov.6.11, וּבָֽא כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵאשֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹֽרְךָ֗ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן, petuchah-closed in WLC (pmarks_Prov.json PE at Prov.6.11; tier-3, single witness), sharing no skeleton token with 6:12, the address mode shifting from second-person imperative and interrogative to third-person portrait; the following unit opens at oshb:Prov.6.16, שֶׁשׁ הֵ֭נָּה שָׂנֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע תועבות תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת נַפְשֽׁוֹ, the six-and-seven numerical formula (1 K/Q note there too, the inline ketiv תועבות before the qere תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת), sharing no skeleton token with 6:15, which is itself petuchah-closed (PE at Prov.6.15; tier-3, single witness). The causal opener at 6:15 and the numerical onset at 6:16 decide; the marks corroborate only. Machine witness: check_universals over the shipped row is GREEN, so no digit gate is implicated. Verdict confirm at medium. The proposed type repair (single_proverb, span Prov.6.12-Prov.6.15 unchanged, dependent fields re-opened) is endorsed as a PROPOSAL with this qualification: the precedent was ruled on a two-verse simile in the Hezekiah collection, and applying it to a four-verse portrait in the lecture collection is a ruling applied rather than a byte fact, so the owner may alternatively type the portrait as wisdom_poem under the closed vocabulary; either way the shipped rejection of single_proverb on verse count cannot stand, and proverb_cluster does not describe these bytes.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, object named first. The row's two verses at byte tier: oshb:Prov.16.10, קֶ֤סֶם עַֽל שִׂפְתֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לֹ֣א יִמְעַל פִּֽיו; oshb:Prov.16.11, פֶּ֤לֶס וּמֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭שְׁפָּט לַֽיהוָ֑ה מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ כָּל אַבְנֵי כִֽיס. The auditor's byte facts all verify: בְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט and מִ֭שְׁפָּט are distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (במשפט in 4 verses book-wide: Prov.16.10, 18.5, 24.23, 29.4; bare משפט in 12: Prov.2.8, 8.20, 12.5, 13.23, 16.8, 16.11, 17.23, 19.28, 21.7, 21.15, 28.5, 29.26), the seam Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11 shares no word-bound skeleton token, the bare form stands two verses earlier as מִשְׁפָּֽט at oshb:Prov.16.8, and the 16:11 token re-sweeps at 1 verse byte tier and 13 accent-stripped including Prov.16.10. The inference built on them does not verify. First, the match is not the hazard catalog's contained-substring trap (a different lexeme sharing letters, as כמה inside חכמה): the bet on the 16:10 form is a proclitic preposition on the same noun, so the two verses share one content lexeme, mishpat, in prefixed and bare forms - a lexical catchword under the campaign's own definition, not a false hit. Second, the corpus does not apply a word-bound-only seam metric: the adjacent row spanning Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 rests on the royal noun across the word-bound-empty seam Prov.16.13|Prov.16.14 (מְ֭לָכִים plural against מֶ֥לֶךְ singular), the row spanning Prov.18.18-Prov.18.19 rests on a bare form against a waw-prefixed qere, and the row spanning Prov.15.31-Prov.15.33 links מ֭וּסָר to מוּסַ֣ר at skeleton tier only; the rows spanning Prov.16.1 and Prov.16.9 refused the 16:1-16:9 envelope because the only recurring token there is the divine name, which they discount as non-content (the bare word-bound token alone stands in 70 verses book-wide), plus three fully empty seams - a different test from the one this row faces. Third, the mishpat object is more distinctive than either the row or the finding states: the contiguous-skeleton sweep returns 20 verses book-wide (sweep.py --skel, verse count) with exactly two adjacent pairs, Prov.2.8|Prov.2.9 in the lectures and Prov.16.10|Prov.16.11, so within the Solomon collection Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16 this seam is the sole adjacent recurrence of the lexeme among its 12 verses there; and the owner-ruled strategy itself names a kings run at 16:10-15 as a cluster candidate, so it contemplates 16:10 and 16:11 inside a multi-verse unit. The cluster therefore has byte-grounded cohesion named in its rationale, which is what the collection's granularity law requires, and the filed high (a load-bearing defect: a cluster with no byte cohesion) is not supported. What is defective, and medium: the rationale presents the object as 'the shared noun' with only a within-span digit ('sweep: 2 consecutive verses'), never states that the two forms are distinct word-bound tokens, names no tier, and omits the book-wide and collection digits that actually distinguish the pair; and strongest_rejected_alternative rejects only the forward extension and never states or rejects the collection's default single_proverb atomization, the mandated rival for every proverb_cluster row. Downgrade to medium. Both sides of every seam the proposal touches, at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.16.9, לֵ֣ב אָ֭דָם יְחַשֵּׁ֣ב דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יָכִ֥ין צַעֲדֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.16.10; the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.16.12, תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת מְ֭לָכִים עֲשׂ֣וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע כִּ֥י בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה יִכּ֥וֹן כִּסֵּֽא, shares none with oshb:Prov.16.11 (the verb עֲשׂ֣וֹת and the noun מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗הוּ are different lexemes of one root); the interior seam carries the mishpat lexeme. The governing rule is the collection's catchword law, and by it the outer edges are empty either way while the interior seam is the one place in the collection where the lexeme recurs in adjacent verses. Span ruling: decline_proposal. Retiring the pair is not byte-compelled: it would dissolve a byte-true catchword on the strength of a word-bound-only metric the corpus applies nowhere else, and it would leave מֶ֑לֶךְ at oshb:Prov.16.10 as an unpaired royal-noun verse directly before the kings run, reopening the seam that the rows spanning Prov.16.10-Prov.16.11 and Prov.16.12-Prov.16.15 currently argue coherently (each states from bytes why 16:11 carries no royal noun and why 16:10 is bound forward by mishpat). The auditor's alternative remedy is the byte-supported one and is endorsed as a field-repair proposal only: re-cut the rationale to name the object as one lexeme in prefixed and bare forms that are distinct word-bound tokens, carry the digits above (4 and 12 word-bound; 20 contiguous with two adjacent pairs book-wide, one in this collection), and state and reject the single_proverb atomization on those grounds. For owner triage: a one-link catchword cluster is the class the strategy expects to hold at lower confidence, so the row's medium sits at the top of its honest range.

items.claim: The rejected-alternative's ground that the second verse is built to invert the first word-for-word is undercut by an undisclosed byte fact: that verse's whole first colon stands byte-identically elsewhere in the book with no such antithesis.
items.grounds: Prov.18.11's first colon, words 1-4 to the etnahta, reads ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ. The colon the row treats as purpose-built to invert its neighbour is therefore a stock colon of the collection, and the row discloses neither that recurrence nor the near-repeat inside its own chapter at Prov.18.19. The cluster is not destroyed by this: a contiguous-skeleton sweep of the exalted-root returns 3 of 915 verses (Prov.18.10, Prov.18.11, Prov.29.25), and Prov.18.10 with Prov.18.11 is the only adjacent pair among them - וְנִשְׂגָּֽב closing Prov.18.10 against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at Prov.18.11 word 6, rendered “and are safe” at web:Prov.18.10 and “an unscalable wall” at web:Prov.18.11 - and that, not the construct phrase, is the pair's distinctive byte object.
items.proposed_change: Move the cluster's primary warrant onto the exalted-root recurrence across the seam (וְנִשְׂגָּֽב at Prov.18.10 word 8 against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at Prov.18.11 word 6; contiguous-skeleton sweep 3 of 915 verses, the book's only adjacent pair) and rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to reject independence on that ground rather than on a word-for-word inversion; add an observed_substrate_signals entry disclosing that Prov.18.11's first colon is byte-identical to words 1-4 of Prov.10.15, so the construct phrase is stock and cannot carry a built-to-invert claim, and add oshb:Prov.10.15 to boundary_evidence_refs to mirror the newly argued verse.

adjudication.grounds: Both facts verify at byte tier: words 1-4 of oshb:Prov.18.11, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ, are codepoint-identical to words 1-4 of oshb:Prov.10.15, ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ, where colon B is מְחִתַּ֖ת דַּלִּ֣ים רֵישָֽׁם and no refuge saying precedes; the contiguous-skeleton sweep of those four words returns exactly 2 verses (Prov.10.15, 18.11), word-bound קרית 2 verses (the same two) and contiguous קרית 3 (adding מִקִּרְיַת at oshb:Prov.18.19, the near-repeat inside this chapter). So the colon the row's rejected alternative calls 'built to invert the first's claim word-for-word' is a stock colon of the collection, and no word-for-word inversion exists in any case (the heads and the strength forms differ, as ruled at the companion item). The actual byte device is the one the finding identifies: the exalted root, וְנִשְׂגָּֽב closing oshb:Prov.18.10 (word 8 of 8) against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at word 6 of oshb:Prov.18.11, contiguous skeleton שגב in 3 verses book-wide (Prov.18.10, 18.11, 29.25 - the last as יְשֻׂגָּֽב) with Prov.18.10|Prov.18.11 the sole adjacent pair, rendered “and are safe” (web:Prov.18.10) and “an unscalable wall” (web:Prov.18.11), verbatim against the staged WEB; together with בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ it carries the true-refuge against imagined-refuge antithesis. The rival rejection therefore rests on a mischaracterized device and omits a byte fact that directly undercuts it; the cluster is not destroyed, so the defect is not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Both sides weighed (the same edges as the companion item): oshb:Prov.18.9 shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.18.10 and oshb:Prov.18.11 none with oshb:Prov.18.12, and the adjacent rows state the same, so the pair's edges are coherent; the interior seam carries the exalted-root recurrence and the root-level strength echo. The proposed field repair is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only, with one qualification: making the exalted-root recurrence the primary warrant and the strength root a disclosed secondary echo is right, the 10:15 disclosure and the mirrored oshb:Prov.10.15 reference follow the corpus's refs-mirror rule, and the rewritten rival must reject independence on the adjacent-recurrence ground rather than on any built-to-invert claim, which the bytes cannot support.

items.claim: The row's exactness claims - the same lexeme repeated unchanged, and the exact same inflected form - are false as word-bound identities and name no tier.
items.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.18.18 opens מִ֭דְיָנִים and the qere at Prov.18.19 is וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים, which carries a conjunctive waw and a different accent set. Word-bound skeleton sweeps separate them cleanly: the unprefixed form returns 8 of 915 verses (Prov.6.14, Prov.18.18, Prov.21.9, Prov.21.19, Prov.23.29, Prov.25.24, Prov.26.21, Prov.27.15) and does NOT include Prov.18.19, while the waw-prefixed form returns 1 of 915 verses, Prov.18.19 alone. The row's scribal handling is otherwise exemplary and should be preserved: the staged pmarks inventory records one ketiv/qere note at Prov.18.19, the row discloses ketiv and qere with the single-witness qualifier, and it correctly builds the catchword on the qere while stating the ketiv, which is the honest way to rest a warrant on a K/Q verse.
items.proposed_change: State the recurrence at the tier the bytes support: the same plural noun recurs across the seam with a conjunctive waw and different accentuation - מִ֭דְיָנִים at Prov.18.18 word 1 against the qere וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים at Prov.18.19 word 6 - identical at contiguous-skeleton tier and distinct word-bound (8 of 915 verses for the bare form, 1 of 915 for the waw-prefixed form); delete 'repeated unchanged' and 'the exact same inflected form', or qualify each with that tier and digit.

adjudication.grounds: Spliced at byte tier: oshb:Prov.18.18, מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד; oshb:Prov.18.19, אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת עֹ֑ז ומדונים וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן, where ומדונים is the inline unpointed ketiv and וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים the pointed qere (pmarks_Prov.json: one ketiv/qere note at Prov.18.19, single witness). The auditor's tiers and digits verify: מִ֭דְיָנִים and the qere are distinct word-bound skeleton tokens (the qere adds a conjunctive waw and carries a different accent set, geresh muqdam plus revia against dehi), the word-bound form מדינים stands in 8 verses book-wide (Prov.6.14, 18.18, 21.9, 21.19, 23.29, 25.24, 26.21, 27.15; 6 of them themselves qere readings beside an inline ketiv) and the waw-prefixed form in 1 (Prov.18.19), the seam shares no word-bound skeleton token, and identity holds at the contiguous-skeleton tier, where the sweep returns 9 verses with Prov.18.18|Prov.18.19 the sole adjacent pair - a digit the row does not carry and which strengthens it. The row's 'repeated unchanged' is therefore a verbatim-class claim with no tier named that is false at byte, accent-stripped and word-bound tiers, and 'exact-repetition catchword' reads the same way. Adversarial correction to the finding: 'the exact same inflected form' is not false as morphology - both tokens are the masculine plural absolute of one noun, and a proclitic waw is not an inflection - so the finding overstates by one claim. Severity is downgraded to low: the object (one plural noun recurring across the seam), the qere-built warrant with the ketiv stated and the single-witness qualifier, and the sole-adjacent-pair status are all byte-sound; the row quotes both forms, so the waw and the accent difference are visible to any reader; what is missing is the tier at which 'unchanged' is true (contiguous skeleton) - a tier-naming disclosure shortfall inside a sound warrant, not a defective warrant claim. Both sides weighed at byte tier: the preceding row's closing verse oshb:Prov.18.17, צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ יבא וּבָֽא רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ (its own ketiv יבא beside the qere וּבָֽא, one note in the inventory), shares no word-bound skeleton token with oshb:Prov.18.18 (בְּרִיב֑וֹ and מִ֭דְיָנִים are dispute nouns of different roots), and oshb:Prov.18.19 shares none with the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.18.20, מִפְּרִ֣י פִי אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע; the rows spanning Prov.18.17 and Prov.18.20 reject clustering across these edges, so the pair's edges are coherent on all three rows and the catchword straddles only the interior seam. The proposed field repair (state the recurrence at the tier the bytes support, with the 8-and-1 word-bound digits and the 9-verse contiguous digit, and delete or qualify 'repeated unchanged') is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only, adding that 'the exact same inflected form' may stand if qualified as morphological rather than token identity.

items.claim: The row's self-declared primary warrant, an a-fortiori dependency running across the seam, is byte-false because the particle it rests on is verse-internal, leaving the cluster on a root the row itself concedes is non-exclusive and whose word-bound recurrence binds a non-adjacent verse instead.
items.grounds: The row's device_notes state that the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between the two verses and not on root-exclusivity, and strongest_rejected_alternative grounds that dependency on 'the particle opening 19:7'. Spliced byte-tier, Prov.19.7 reads כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה: it opens on כָּ֥ל, a quantifier, and the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י stands at words 5 and 6 with the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ - so that particle governs the relation between Prov.19.7's own cola, not the relation across the seam, and no particle opens the verse at all. What remains is the friend-root, and word-bound skeleton sweeps show it does not bind this pair: the form at Prov.19.6, הָ֝רֵ֗עַ, is word-bound in 2 of 915 verses (Prov.17.17, Prov.19.6), and the form at Prov.19.7, מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ, is word-bound in 3 of 915 verses (Prov.12.26, Prov.19.4, Prov.19.7); the two sets do not intersect, and the word-bound recurrence actually links Prov.19.7 to the NON-adjacent Prov.19.4, which the row itself discloses while still carrying the cluster. OW-3 both-sides on both seams: at the leading seam the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.5 reads עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט and the row's opening verse Prov.19.6 reads רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי נָדִ֑יב וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן, sharing no word-bound skeleton token; at the trailing seam the row's closing verse Prov.19.7 and the following row's opening verse Prov.19.8, קֹֽנֶה לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא טֽוֹב, likewise share none - so both outer edges are clean and the only live boundary is the seam INSIDE the row, which carries no word-bound shared token either. C2's ruled default is single_proverb with proverb_cluster only on byte-grounded cohesion named in the rationale; the cohesion named here is a discourse dependency the bytes place inside one verse, on top of a root the row itself declines to call exclusive.
items.proposed_change: Retire the two-verse cluster and atomize to the collection default: one row Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and one row Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7, both unit_type single_proverb, parent_collection unchanged at C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16, confidence re-opened as a dependent field of the driver swap along with observed_substrate_signals and strongest_rejected_alternative. The Prov.19.7 row then carries the a-fortiori structure as its OWN internal device (אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6, etnahta on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ at word 9) plus its scribal disclosures (the staged inventory records one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg at Prov.19.7, single-witness, the paseq layer count-only), and discloses as texture the word-bound friend-token it shares with the non-adjacent Prov.19.4 (3 of 915 verses). The Prov.19.6 row carries its own friend-token (2 of 915 verses word-bound) and the gift-giver theme it shares with Prov.19.4 as texture, never as cluster grounds. This is a candidate proposal for owner triage and applies nothing to any shipped corpus.

adjudication.grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The row's self-declared primary warrant (device_notes: the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7; strongest_rejected_alternative: 'the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6') fails at byte tier. Prov.19.7 spliced from verse_map_oshb.json is כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה - fourteen whitespace tokens including the inline ketiv/qere pair לא לוֹ at words 12-13 - opening on the quantifier כָּ֥ל at word 1, with the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6 and the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ; the particle therefore relates the verse's own first clause, כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ (words 1-4), to its second, מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ (words 7-9), and no particle opens the verse, so the cross-seam grammatical dependency the row rests on is byte-false and, by the row's own words, load-bearing: high under the severity law, exactly as filed. Testing the row against the finding: the residual friend-root is real but does not bind the pair at token tier. Word-bound consonantal-skeleton sweeps (whitespace-token equality, verse counts) give 19:6's הָ֝רֵ֗עַ (skeleton הרע) 2 of 915 verses (Prov.17.17, Prov.19.6) and 19:7's מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ (skeleton מרעהו) 3 of 915 (Prov.12.26, Prov.19.4, Prov.19.7), disjoint sets, and the skeleton token sets of Prov.19.6 and Prov.19.7 intersect in the empty set even with function words counted.
